newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Hong Kong airport charges will hit traffic - IATA.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong airport charges will hit traffic - IATA.

text.p: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) said Hong Kong, now a major air cargo hub, could lose a million passengers a year if moves to introduce high airline charges at its new Chek Lap Kok airport went ahead.
IATA, which says Chek Lap Kok (CLK) risks becoming an airport for the rich, urged Hong Kong's Airport Authority to reconsider its plans on charges in a statement on Tuesday.
The world airline body has said a doubling of charges would cost an extra $150 to a family of four travelling out of the British colony, which will be taken over by China on July 1.

IATA called on Hong Kong to use revenues from the Kai Tak airport to help offset costs of CLK, due to open in April 1998, and urged a resolution to the problem at March 13 talks between Hong Kong Airport Authority and airline representatives.

IATA says research showed Boeing 747 landing fees at CLK could amount to US$12,000. This would be four times the present level and compares to the existing most expensive landing fee of US$9,000 at Osaka's Kansai airport.
Industry sources say airlines with hub operations based in Hong Kong -- Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines -- would be worst affected by the new charges.

High charges would also encourage much greater use of the rival Pearl River Estuary airports, especially for cargo operations, they say. These airports are at Shenzen, near to Hong Kong, Macau and Zhuhai across the Pearl River, and both the existing and planned new Guangzhou airports.
